clue.text: Touch up member of band?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for the band member is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tuba is an instrument in a brass band, so a member of it

explanation.surface: A musician asks whether to retouch a photo of a bandmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch up' looks like one phrase meaning retouch, but 'up' belongs to the wordplay. 'Member of band' gives TUBA, which 'up' turns into ABUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that abut are in contact along a border, so the verb is a synonym of touch.

clue.text: Group of stars penning intro to Save a Prayer

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the constellation's name holds the letter inside it

parts.note: Orion, the Hunter, is a constellation, a group of stars

indicators.note: the intro to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Save a Prayer is a Duran Duran single; the clue pictures a star-studded group recording it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' puts S, the first letter of 'Save', inside ORION.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old literary word for a prayer, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Upset at teary Simon Le Bon interrupting where some tracks end

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the singer's surname goes into the middle of the mixed letters
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of at teary and the singer's first name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Simon Le Bon, Duran Duran's singer, barges in on someone upset and tearful.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer's name splits: his first name joins the mixed letters and his surname does the interrupting. The answer is a London rail terminus, so railway tracks end there.
explanation.definitionFit: This London terminus is where the Chiltern line's railway lines stop, a descriptive definition of a terminal station.

clue.text: Bird left pub before start of extra time

indicators.note: before puts the preceding pieces ahead of the last one

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the pub before extra time starts in the football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A linnet is a small brown finch, so this is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Sex appeal wearing kinky undies turned into a single piece

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the shuffled underwear goes round the other piece
kinky means twisted, so the letters of undies are rearranged

parts.note: IT is an old slang word for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Sex appeal in kinky underwear is a racy picture that suddenly ends in an engineering phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is old slang, from the 1920s 'It girl' Clara Bow.
explanation.definitionFit: To unitise something is to make it into one combined unit, which is a single piece.

clue.text: Crazy Duran Duran fans go wild — fee for picture

indicators.note: crazy means wildly disordered, so all the letters that follow up to the dash are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild Duran Duran fans pay a fee for a picture, presumably a signed photo of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go wild' looks like the anagram signal but its letters are part of the fodder; 'Crazy' does that job, mixing all twenty-three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture is a common word for a film or movie, and this is a 1994 British romantic comedy.

clue.text: One inside models for covers

indicators.note: inside says the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: copies are replicas or models of an original
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: One person among the models is arranging magazine covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' tempts a solver toward I, but here it is the article meaning one.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopies are overhead coverings over beds or thrones, so covers is a synonym.

clue.text: British like supporters

parts.note: as can mean like, as in white as snow

explanation.surface: A short claim that British people like supporters, perhaps football fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassieres support the bust, so they are supporters in a literal undergarment sense.

clue.text: Wild Boys, initially song and note getting stick at first

indicators.note: at first puts the stick piece ahead of everything else

parts.note: a bar is a rod or stick

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: Wild Boys is a Duran Duran hit; the clue reads like a description of how the song begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild Boys' looks like one title, but 'Wild' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarian as an adjective means uncivilised and savage, a synonym for wild.

clue.text: Playing song live

parts.note: a show that is on is playing
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A band is playing a song live.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast going out as it happens is live, the radio and TV sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Attractive model with a pen

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T can stand for model
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: An attractive model is posing with a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' is not a fashion model but the Ford Model T, giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasty is slang for sexually attractive, as well as its usual sense of delicious.

clue.text: Rejection for Duran Duran song? America is infamous

parts.note: no is a refusal or rejection
to and for can both mean towards, as in heading to or for home
Rio is a 1982 Duran Duran hit
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: Turning down a Duran Duran song might make you infamous in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself another Duran Duran single, making the question mark a playful nod.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, the same sense as the adjective in the clue.

clue.text: Admirer hit part of car

parts.note: a fan is an admirer
to belt is to hit hard

explanation.surface: An admirer gets hit, perhaps by a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The belt driving the radiator fan in an engine is one component of a car.

clue.text: Bored following half of band, ran off during record

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: during says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: off means removed, so those letters go from the name
half of takes the first half of the doubled band name

parts.note: Duran Duran is the band behind the puzzle's theme

explanation.surface: A bored fan follows half the band, who ran off during a recording session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran off' is not a verb phrase in the story but a deletion: 'ran' is the letters removed from the half name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tired and weary of a situation is bored by it, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: See 3
Mutation of organism to one studying land?

indicators.note: a mutation is a change in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A biology note about a mutated organism turning into something else.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in soil science and crop production is someone who studies land, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Cheeky? Section of arena talking

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone in part of a stadium is being cheeky, chatting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky' is used in its literal sense of the buttocks: nates are the buttocks, and the adjective here relates to them.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare word means relating to the buttocks, so cheeky in the bottom sense is a playful synonym.

clue.text: Still in party? Slip away after girl's left

indicators.note: after places the slipping-away piece behind the girl's initial

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the left of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to go is to slip away or leave

explanation.surface: Someone at a party wonders about slipping away once a girl has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like departed but picks the first letter, G, of girl's.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is to stay still and hidden, so the word is an idiomatic synonym of motionless.

clue.text: Film men wrestling with girls

indicators.note: wrestling bodies are tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Men wrestling with girls sounds like a scene in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1984 Joe Dante comedy horror is an example of a film.

clue.text: Hunk from poster after women

indicators.note: after places the poster piece behind the other

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, which a poster may be

explanation.surface: Women swooning after a hunk on a poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunk' suggests a handsome man, but it means a chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A wad is a lump or chunk of something, so a hunk in that sense.

clue.text: See 6
Place again on the box

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
the box is British slang for television, and a TV is a set

explanation.surface: Something is put back on the television.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset is to set or put back in position once more, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Put on pressure to split, film's captured

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: captured says the film's letters are held inside the other piece

parts.note: to rend is to tear or split
ET is the Spielberg film; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Pressure causes a film crew to split, and the moment is caught on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'film's' stands for 'is', so the film is the thing captured.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on an act is to feign or fake it, a phrasal synonym of the verb.

clue.text: See 6
Flab reduced in work out

parts.note: flab is body fat

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: at home means in, so home stands for in

explanation.surface: Flab reduced by a gym workout: a fitness picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' looks like exercise but means understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom a problem is to understand or figure it out, a synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Artist and band full of enthusiasm

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: An artist and a band are full of enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring to go means eager and keen, so the word is an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Steal girl? Fancy one seeing someone highly sensitive?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A would-be suitor asks about stealing a girl he fancies, who is seeing someone touchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing someone' suggests dating, but it is a doctor seeing a patient with reactions to pollen or nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical specialist treats patients whose bodies overreact to things, so they see highly sensitive people.

clue.text: See 6
See 26
Planet Earth features one topless star dressing

indicators.note: features means includes, so the planet and Earth letters hold the others

parts.note: Mars is a planet
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a hero is the star of a story

explanation.surface: Planet Earth is a Duran Duran song; the clue pictures a topless star dressing for the video.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planet Earth' looks like one song title but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink sauce of mayonnaise and ketchup goes on prawn cocktail, so it is a dressing.

clue.text: Old lovers need tablet — nooky when erect?

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

indicators.note: erect means upright, so in a down clue the word for nooky reads upwards

parts.note: nooky is slang for sex

explanation.surface: Ex-partners needing a pill to perform: a cheeky joke about ageing lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Former partners are called by this short informal plural, so old lovers is a synonym.

clue.text: Drops in drink revenue primarily from boozers

indicators.note: from says the letter is taken away from the drinkers

parts.note: drunks are heavy drinkers

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of revenue

explanation.surface: Revenue from pubs falls as people drink less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' looks like a fall in sales but means plunges a biscuit into tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To dunk is to dip food into a drink, so it describes dropping something into it.

clue.text: Wit and idols seen playing around circuit

indicators.note: around says the idols go round the circuit letter

parts.note: idols are gods, false or otherwise
a circuit is a loop, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: playing means fooling about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pop idols are seen playing around the gig circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit can mean common sense or intelligence, as in having the wits to do something.
